annotation_description: In a 4-player Commander game, choosing yourself as the starting player means you go first but miss your first draw step. With Zurgo Helmsmasher as commander (an aggressive Mardu deck that wants to attack early), going first has some merit for tempo. However, in multiplayer Commander, going later is often advantageous because you get to draw an extra card and see what opponents are doing before committing. The conventional wisdom in 4-player games is that going last (or at least not first) is often better since you gain card advantage and political information. That said, going first with an aggressive commander like Zurgo can be defensible for early pressure, so this is debatable rather than a clear mistake.

message: Choose which mana to produce from Graven Cairns (tapping to pay for a spell)
annotation_description: DSV3 Hist activated Elixir of Immortality on turn 2 with an empty graveyard, gaining 5 life but shuffling away the artifact for essentially no value. The Elixir's primary purpose is to recycle your graveyard back into your library, but with no cards in graveyard, the activation only gains 5 life at the cost of losing the artifact permanently (until drawn again). Additionally, they used colorless mana from Graven Cairns when they could have used it more efficiently, but the bigger issue is the pointless Elixir activation itself.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Myriad Landscape
chosen_display: 2. {2}, {T}, Sacrifice Myriad Landscape: Search your library for up to two basic land cards that share a land type, put them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.
annotation_description: Activating Myriad Landscape on turn 2 means sacrificing a land and paying 2 mana, leaving Kimi with no untapped lands this turn and getting two tapped Forests. While this ramps, it's premature — Kimi has two Forests in hand to play naturally over the next turns. The hand has Essence Warden (1 mana) and Swiftfoot Boots (2 mana) as early plays. By cracking Myriad Landscape now instead of playing a Forest from hand, Kimi loses tempo: they could have played Forest, then had 3 mana available (or 2 untapped + Myriad Landscape for future use). Playing a Forest from hand first and saving Myriad Landscape for a later turn when there are fewer land drops in hand would be more efficient, allowing earlier deployment of Essence Warden or Swiftfoot Boots.

Knight of the White Orchid's ETB trigger will not activate because no opponent controls more lands than DSV3 Hist (who has 3 lands, tied with GPT4om's 3 and ahead of the others' 2). This wastes the card's primary value as a ramp spell. Waiting to deploy Knight when behind on lands would extract more value.

With 3 mana available on turn 3, casting Swiftfoot Boots (2 mana) leaves only 1 mana open with no creature to equip. Essence Warden (1 mana) is a strong early play in multiplayer that gains incremental life from every creature entering the battlefield, and playing it first would allow the remaining 2 mana to cast Swiftfoot Boots as well - getting both onto the battlefield this turn. Alternatively, playing Essence Warden + Elvish Skysweeper would develop the board with two creatures. Playing Boots alone with no creatures to protect is low-impact.

Casting Masked Admirers (4 mana) before combat is suboptimal when holding Beastmaster Ascension. The Admirers could have been cast post-combat, and there's no particular reason to play it pre-combat since it doesn't have haste and won't affect combat this turn. More importantly, with only 4 mana available (3 Forests + Myriad Landscape), casting Masked Admirers uses all mana, preventing other plays like Elvish Skysweeper + Sylvan Safekeeper or Beastmaster Ascension (3 mana). Beastmaster Ascension at 3 mana would have been more impactful since Essence Warden could attack this turn to start accumulating quest counters, and it leaves 1 mana open for Sylvan Safekeeper or Elvish Skysweeper. The card draw from Admirers is nice but Beastmaster Ascension is a more powerful engine card that benefits from being deployed early.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Attacking DSV3 Hist with a 1/1 Essence Warden is essentially pointless - it deals only 1 damage and risks losing a valuable lifegain engine if DSV3 Hist has the 4/4 Knight of the White Orchid (with +1/+1 counters making it a 4/4) available to block, which would kill the Essence Warden. DSV3 Hist has a Knight of the White Orchid with two +1/+1 counters (4/4) that is tapped, so it can't block this turn. However, Essence Warden is more valuable as a lifegain engine in a multiplayer game than dealing 1 damage. Additionally, attacking into DSV3 Hist draws political attention when Kimi25 Story has a relatively modest board position. The Masked Admirers is summoning sick so can't attack, but sending a key utility creature into combat for 1 damage is questionable value.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Myriad Landscape
chosen_display: 2. {2}, {T}, Sacrifice Myriad Landscape: Search your library for up to two basic land cards that share a land type, put them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.
annotation_description: Kimi25 Story activated Myriad Landscape using all available mana without first casting a 1-mana creature. They had Sylvan Safekeeper (G) and Elvish Skysweeper (G) in hand, and could have cast one using 1 Forest, then still activated Myriad Landscape with the remaining 2 Forests + tapping Myriad Landscape. This would have developed the board further and triggered Essence Warden for 1 life.

Played Oran-Rief, the Vastwood (enters tapped) instead of Gargoyle Castle (enters untapped), and then failed to cast a 1-drop creature (Elvish Skysweeper or Sylvan Safekeeper) with the untapped Forest. Playing Gargoyle Castle would have provided 2 mana: enough to cast a creature AND equip Swiftfoot Boots, significantly developing the board. Even with Oran-Rief, they should have cast a 1-drop with the untapped Forest.

message: Choose spell or ability to play: Slippery Karst
chosen_display: 2. Cycling {2} ({2}, Discard this card: Draw a card.)
annotation_description: Cycling Slippery Karst instead of playing it as a land is questionable. Kimi25 Story has 7 lands on the battlefield (3 tapped, 4 untapped) and expensive cards in hand like Siege Behemoth (7 mana) and Terastodon (8 mana). Playing Slippery Karst as a tapped land would accelerate toward casting these powerful threats. Cycling draws a random card but delays the mana development needed for the hand's payoffs. Additionally, cycling triggers Grok4 Johnny's Centaur Vinecrasher graveyard ability, potentially giving an opponent back a threat. The draw from cycling is unlikely to be better than the guaranteed mana acceleration toward Siege Behemoth or Terastodon.

message: Select a player, planeswalker, or battle to attack
annotation_description: Kimi25 Story is attacking GPT4om Rookie with a 1/1 Sylvan Safekeeper. While GPT4om Rookie has no blockers, the 1 damage is minimal. The choice of attack target is debatable - DSV3 Hist at 36 life has a Blood Artist (0/1) that could block but is more threatening long-term, while Grok4 Johnny at 37 life has no creatures to block. However, the real consideration is whether attacking with Sylvan Safekeeper is wise at all, since it's a valuable utility creature that provides shroud protection by sacrificing lands. Losing it in combat (if somehow blocked or removed) would be costly. That said, with no blockers available from GPT4om Rookie, the attack is safe. The 1 damage is nearly meaningless though, and the Beastmaster Ascension quest counter is the real value. With only 1 creature attacking, it will take many turns to reach 7 counters, making this a very slow plan. The choice of GPT4om Rookie over other targets is reasonable since they have no blockers.

Cast Timberwatch Elf (a 1/2 that gives +1/+1 with only itself as an Elf) without first playing a land, when playing Forest first would have enabled casting Soul of the Harvest (6/6 trample + card draw engine) or Siege Behemoth (7/4 hexproof). Timberwatch Elf is extremely low impact with no board presence.

message: Pick triggered ability (goes to the stack first)
annotation_description: Blood Artist's 1 damage was directed at Kimi25 Story who is at 41 life (the highest life total), when GPT4om Rookie is at only 15 life and would be a much more impactful target for incremental damage.

With 7 mana available (and Gargoyle Castle as an unplayed land drop for 8 total), Kimi25 Story cast a 1/1 Sylvan Ranger instead of deploying a major threat. The reasoning cited Soul of the Harvest triggering, but Soul of the Harvest is in hand, not on the battlefield. The optimal line would be to play Gargoyle Castle first, then cast Soul of the Harvest (6 mana) + Sylvan Ranger (2 mana) to get the 6/6 trampler AND draw a card from it, or at minimum cast Siege Behemoth (7 mana) as a 7/4 hexproof threat.

Kimi25 Story has 7 lands (6 Forests + Oran-Rief, the Vastwood) and passed without casting anything. They have several castable spells: Sylvan Ranger (1G), Siege Behemoth (5GG - exactly 7 mana), or Soul of the Harvest (4GG - 6 mana). Soul of the Harvest would provide card draw for future creatures, and Siege Behemoth is a powerful 7/4 with hexproof. They also have Gargoyle Castle which could be played as a land drop if they haven't made one yet. Instead they passed and had to discard down to 7, losing a card for nothing.

Discarded Soul of the Harvest based on the false belief it was already on the battlefield (it was not). Soul of the Harvest would have been valuable with a hand full of creatures (Sylvan Ranger, Masked Admirers, Siege Behemoth, Terastodon) to trigger its card draw ability. The reasoning was factually wrong about the game state.

Kimi25 Story has 6 mana available (5 Forests + Oran-Rief) and passed without casting anything. Sylvan Ranger costs only 1G and would fetch a basic land, helping ramp toward the expensive spells in hand (Terastodon, Wave of Vitriol, Siege Behemoth). It also triggers Beastmaster Ascension on future attacks and puts a body on the board. Additionally, they have 8 cards in hand and will need to discard to hand size, so casting Sylvan Ranger would avoid wasting a card to discard. Instead, they passed and discarded a card for no benefit.

Discarded Sylvan Ranger instead of Masked Admirers. Masked Admirers has a built-in ability to return from graveyard to hand whenever you cast a creature spell (for {G}{G}), making it the ideal discard since you can recover it later. Sylvan Ranger's land-fetching ETB, while less impactful at 7 lands, still has more 'lost value' when discarded since it cannot be recurred.

Kimi25 Story passed with 6 untapped mana and Grim Flowering in hand, which would draw 7 cards (7 creature cards in graveyard). They have zero creatures on board and need to rebuild. Even Elvish Visionary or Masked Admirers would have been productive plays. Passing here wastes an entire turn's worth of mana with powerful options available.

Cast Terastodon before playing a land for the turn. Also, the reasoning references 'Soul of the Harvest triggers' but Soul of the Harvest is in the graveyard, not on the battlefield. The land drop should come first as it's free mana/value that could matter later.

Kimi25 Story selected their own Beastmaster Ascension as a target for removal/bounce, destroying a key piece of their own win condition that they've been building quest counters on. There were opponent permanents available to target instead.
